paper_title: Forwarding Packets Greedily on the Line
statement: 5 Open Problem We conjecture that Greedy has a constant competitive ratio, possibly 2, for online packet routing even when packet lengths are unbounded. A difficulty in extending Lemma 6 to packets of length greater than two is that the packets delayed by Opt, namely those in G \ O, need not all be located on one router. In the worst case, they could be distributed evenly across the preceding routers, for example. The maximum packet length may therefore enter the competitive analysis, perhaps only through an additive constant.
context: Thus, by Lemma 10, Alg, being a 4/3-competitive algorithm, has in expectation more than (1/3 − ε/2) · Ui packets left to process on router i at time t. Releasing Ui additional packets at time t that need to be processed on router i therefore gives Alg an expected cost greater than (4/3 − ε/2) · Ui . In contrast, the definition of critical guarantees that Off, and hence Opt, can schedule I (i) together with these additional packets with cost Ui , because no packet remains to be processed on router i at time t. Since ℓ, and hence Ui , can be chosen arbitrarily large, this contradicts the assumption that Alg is (4/3 − ε)-competitive. ◀ 5 Open Problem We conjecture that Greedy has a constant competitive ratio, possibly 2, for online packet routing even when packet lengths are unbounded. The maximum packet length may therefore enter the competitive analysis, perhaps only through an additive constant.
